Security PASS-WITH-NOTES: PR #293, final round 2
Head: 0a7ff6de7aea496025df7c5a5f3ba4a792448198
Base: 288d0d078fe0ef524a3e56c87a94ae8f6a382d88
Prior reviewed head: d17dae35a62fd7fbf88a17f230a0603d77fafdc4
Request: 01a1f96f-c8d4-7251-9615-30669c5c8bea

S293-001 CLOSED. No new security vulnerability found in the round-2 repair.
At justfile:755-758, the helper uses quoted native -L "$label" for a named server, or no socket flag otherwise. It no longer synthesizes a default/named socket into -S. This restores tmux's directory-owner validation for named/default resolution and closes the round-1 cross-user environment-disclosure finding.

The ownership-check mechanism was verified against official tmux 3.6a at commit cc117b5048f77a4842820f8ebbe3a86e5c077224, tmux.c:211-228,518-534. An inherited TMUX path remains trusted caller environment under C33; it is not independently directory-owner-checked.

Requested inside-other-TMUX condition:
Without a label, the helper targets the caller's TMUX, not an independently discovered old-daemon server. The daemon resolves from its own startup environment (crates/tmux/src/control.rs:676-690). With a label, native -L takes precedence over TMUX.
Therefore differing caller/daemon environments CAN target another server; this review does not certify that such a mismatch is impossible. This is the inherited, nonblocking R1 targeting limitation, not a new round-2 regression: the R1 helper at d17dae35 already selected ${TMUX%%,*} (that head's justfile:749-754), and the R1 security verdict recorded the limitation. C33 trusts same-user environment and C34 does not add another hardening round for it.

The new refusal/deadline logic adds no security finding in this review. The correctness and performance owners retain P293-001, disposition, timing, mutation and live-cost proof. This security verdict does not substitute for their verdicts or claim independent real-tmux timing measurements.

Evidence:
- Read-only source review of the two R2 commits and relevant socket resolution.
- Supplemental in-memory shell-function dispatch assertions passed: default/outside-TMUX and inside-other-TMUX/no-label produce set-option -t _pij: destroy-unattached off; inside-other-TMUX/named produces -L fleet set-option -t _pij: destroy-unattached off. No real tmux or daemon was invoked by this supplemental check.
- Repository Rust fixtures are source plus exact-head CI proof only. No local Rust build/test or live two-server smoke was run by the security review.
- just pr-freeze 293: FINAL at this exact head both at entry and immediately before publication.
- gh run view 44756157877 --json headSha,conclusion,jobs: success at this exact head. check (22), check (24), rust-lint and rust-test passed; both Node jobs include passing typecheck, lint, npm test and native contracts. The latest Delivers job succeeded in run 44756165095, superseding an earlier cancelled job.
- harness boot --json: advisory ready:false because node_modules is absent.
- harness checks --quick --json: exit 1; missing local tsx/vitest tools and an incompatible ambient Biome prevented a green local gate. pij-skill, native contracts and SDK contract passed. Heavy Rust, route-inventory and smoke stages were skipped, not passed.
- C25 respected: no dependency install or symlink. Both the pinned checkout and source tree remain clean. No credentials inspected and no live daemon/server altered.

Harness friction / magic wand: a read-only gate should verify local executable readiness and report exact-head CI receipts without falling back to incompatible ambient tools. This was captured as a harness observation; no source changes were made in the review worktree.

This is a scoped final-round security PASS-WITH-NOTES, not a declaration that the unavailable local full ship gate passed. The security/293 holding remains until the PR merges.
